hints: Notice the puzzle in the stem: total energy released is fixed for each nucleus, yet the $\beta^-$ kinetic energy is not fixed.
Recall that energy must still be conserved, so if the $\beta^-$ particle sometimes carries less kinetic energy, another emitted particle must carry away the remainder.
Think about the $\beta^-$ decay equation $n \rightarrow p + e^- + \bar{\nu}_e$ and how sharing energy between two light emitted particles gives a continuous spectrum.
walkthrough: Identify the given facts: each decaying nucleus releases the same total energy, but the emitted $\beta^-$ particle shows kinetic energies from near zero up to a maximum value.
State the governing rule: total energy, including mass energy and kinetic energy, must be conserved in the decay.
If only the daughter nucleus and the $\beta^-$ particle were produced, the $\beta^-$ particle would carry essentially the same kinetic energy each time, as in alpha decay with discrete energies.
In $\beta^-$ decay a third particle, an electron antineutrino, is also emitted: $n \rightarrow p + \beta^- + \bar{\nu}_e$.
The fixed released energy is therefore shared between the kinetic energies of the $\beta^-$ particle and the antineutrino in all possible proportions, producing the continuous $\beta^-$ spectrum.
This sharing explanation matches the statement about energy taken by an emitted antineutrino. This is option B.

options.A: Recoil of the daughter nucleus does occur but it is very small and almost the same each time, so it cannot produce the large continuous range of $\beta^-$ kinetic energies.
options.B: The total released energy is shared in varying proportions between the $\beta^-$ particle and the antineutrino, so the $\beta^-$ kinetic energy varies continuously up to a maximum.
options.C: The $\beta^-$ particle is created in the decay, but its rest mass energy is the same for every decay and so cannot explain a continuous range of kinetic energy.
options.D: Beta-minus decay converts a neutron into a proton, but the nucleon already exists as part of the change and no extra nucleon is created using variable energy.
